title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Secure SDLC, Incident Response, and Evidence Workflows
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s security and compliance controls and operational procedures across the following areas: RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and handling of risk & exceptions. It provides prescriptive configurations, ownership, escalation paths, and evidence-gathering checklists to support audits and customer assessments.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood-managed services (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, and Private deployments) and internal engineering processes that affect security posture (code repos, CI/CD, infra, and supply chain dependencies). Excludes: third-party customer-managed on-prem components where the customer contract explicitly places responsibility on the customer (see related_pages).

1) RBAC & Authentication

Goal: Ensure least-privilege access across cloud and internal tooling with auditable identity flows.

Key controls:
- Central identity provider: Okta is Redwood’s primary IdP for SSO across GCP/AWS console, internal apps, and CI systems.
- Role model: Use role-based groups mapped to duties rather than individual accounts. Roles include: security-admin, infra-admin, service-operator, developer, support-analyst, read-only-audit.
- Just-in-time elevation: Short-lived elevated roles via AWS IAM Role Sessions or Privileged Access Tool for emergency changes. Elevation requires justification and automatic logging.
- Service-to-service auth: mTLS + workload identities (GCP Workload Identity / AWS IAM Roles for Service Accounts) for internal service calls.
- Multi-factor authentication: Enforced for all human accounts with access to production systems, admin consoles, and sensitive data stores.

Configuration checklist (table represented as text):
- Identity provider: Okta
- MFA: REQUIRED (TOTP + hardware tokens for privileged roles)
- Session lifetime: 1 hour for elevated sessions, 12 hours for standard sessions
- Password policy: N/A (SSO enforced)
- Service account key rotation: 90 days
- Admin group membership review: quarterly

Process:
1. Role creation/change request in the access request tracker (Jira project: SEC-ACCESS).
2. Approver: role owner (security for privileged roles; team lead for team-scoped roles).
3. Automated provisioning via Terraform + OPA policies; manual approvals where required.

2) Audit Logging

Goal: Capture sufficient telemetry to support detection, forensics, and compliance evidence while balancing storage costs.

Logging sources and retention: 
- Authentication & access logs (IdP): retained 3 years 
- Cloud admin activity (GCP/AWS console/API): retained 2 years in immutable storage
- Application access and API request logs (hosted API control plane): 13 months (default), 3 years for enterprise customers by contract add-on
- System and kernel logs for infra fleet: 90 days on hot storage, archive to cold storage for 24 months
- Audit trail for RBAC changes (group membership, policy updates): 7 years

Logging standards and structure:
- All logs MUST include timestamp (ISO8601), actor (principal_id), action, resource identifier, outcome (success/failure), and request_id/correlation_id.
- Sensitive fields (PII, secrets, full prompts containing customer data) MUST be redacted at ingestion or encrypted using customer-managed keys depending on deployment type.
- Tamper-evidence: logs stored in append-only buckets with object immutability/enforced retention and checksums.

Search and retention policies:
- Security team maintains a dedicated SIEM (Splunk/Google Chronicle) with role-limited dashboards.
- Retention overrides for investigations: follow legal hold process (see Appendix – Evidence Hold Procedure).

3) Data Residency & Retention

Principles:
- Customers choose regional residency at onboarding (US, EU, APAC). Customer data and prompt/response traces for hosted deployments are stored only in selected regions.
- Minimal retention by default: only metadata required for billing and debugging retained beyond evaluation windows.

Default retention windows (hosted):
- Short-term request traces / KV cache: 30 days
- Full request/response traces (for quality/regression): 90 days
- Billing and metering data: 7 years
- Backups for control plane config: 3 years

Customer-specific controls:
- Contractual retention overrides and data deletion workflows for enterprise customers: documented in the customer contract and executed via support runbook.
- For private deployments, retention and residency are configured on the customer-managed infra; Redwood provides guidance and automation templates.

4) Secure SDLC

Objective: Ensure software that reaches production has passed security gates, automated checks, and necessary approvals.

Required gates for every merging change: 
- Pre-commit: dependency vulnerability scanning (dependabot/Snyk), license checks.
- CI pipeline: static analysis (semgrep), unit tests, linting, and secrets scanning.
- Build: reproducible builds, SBOM generation for service images.
- Pre-merge: automated unit and integration tests + security smoke tests.
- Merge to main: approval from at least one code owner and passing CI. For changes touching security boundary (auth, RBAC, audit, data handling) a security-reviews label triggers a security review (SEC-REVIEW).
- Release: staged rollout (canary, percent rollouts) with automated rollback on error budget/SLO breach.

Developer guidance and checklist (high level):
- Add threat model for new public endpoints and data flows.
- Document data classification & handling for new features.
- Include plan for logging and monitoring for any new stateful components.

5) Incident Response — Security Procedures

Goal: Contain, eradicate, and remediate security incidents with clear ownership and evidence preservation.

Incident levels and SLAs:
- Sev1 (active breach affecting customer data / production control plane compromise): mobilize IR runbook within 30 minutes; exec pager and legal notified within 1 hour.
- Sev2 (suspected compromise, elevated privilege abuse, lateral movement): initial response within 1 hour; containment plan within 6 hours.
- Sev3 (non-production compromise, low-impact vulnerability exploited): acknowledgement within 4 hours.

Key steps (high-level):
1. Detection & triage: Security on-call verifies and assigns severity.
2. Containment: short-lived credentials revoked, affected nodes isolated, network ACLs applied.
3. Evidence preservation: snapshot affected VMs, preserve logs under legal hold, hash and store evidence in evidence vault (immutable).
4. Investigation: timeline reconstruction using audit logs, packet captures (if enabled), and process traces.
5. Remediation: patching, configuration rollbacks, credential rotations, and targeted customer notifications.
6. Post-incident review: produce an incident report with root cause, timeline, impact, and remediation actions.

Communication and escalation:
- Incident commander: security manager on-call.
- L1/L2: SRE + engineering owners.
- Legal & PR: notified for customer-impacting incidents per notification thresholds.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Purpose: Produce consistent, auditable evidence packages for internal audits and customer SOC2/ISO/PA assessments.

Evidence collection checklist (per control family):
- RBAC controls: group membership exports, policy version history, approval records, and periodic review logs.
- Auth & MFA: IdP authentication logs, MFA enforcement policy screenshots, exception tickets.
- Audit logging: retention configuration, sample immutable log objects, SIEM export queries and saved searches.
- Data residency: configuration of region selectors, storage bucket policies, and encryption key metadata.
- SDLC: PR history for release, SBOM, CI pipelines logs, and security review approvals.
- Incident response: incident ticket, evidence vault artifacts, final incident report, and remediation verification checks.

Workflow steps for typical audit request:
1. Audit intake: Security Ops creates an audit bucket & checklist tied to the auditor request ticket.
2. Owner assignment: map controls to control owners (see Ownership & Contacts).
3. Evidence collection: owners dump relevant artifacts into the audit bucket; artifacts are hashed and indexed.
4. Reviewer validation: security reviewer validates completeness and redaction where applicable.
5. Delivery: package created and delivered via secure transfer (encrypted S3 link with expiry or secure portal).

Retention of evidence: evidence packages are retained for the duration specified by the audit engagement (generally 3–7 years) and are subject to the same immutability and access controls as logs.

7) Risk & Exceptions

Policy: Exceptions to baseline controls are allowed only through the formal Risk & Exception process, with documented compensating controls and time-boxed approvals.

Exception lifecycle:
1. Submit exception request in the Risk Register (template: RR-EXC) including: control(s) affected, business justification, proposed compensating controls, and proposed end date.
2. Initial assessment by Control Owner and Security Risk team within 7 business days.
3. Authorization: CISO signs exceptions with residual risk acceptance thresholds; high-risk exceptions require CTO & Legal approval.
4. Mitigation & monitoring: agreed compensating controls implemented and evidence of monitoring submitted monthly.
5. Renewal/closure: exceptions auto-expire; owners must request renewal prior to expiry.

Acceptance criteria for low-risk exceptions (examples):
- Limited-time developer access to a sandbox requiring elevated privileges where no customer data is present and additional monitoring is enabled.

9) Appendix — Configuration Examples & Runbook Snippets

Example: RBAC Terraform snippet (illustrative)
``
resource "okta_group" "service_operators" {
  name        = "service-operator"
  description = "Group for service operators with limited production privileges"
}
```

Evidence hold command (CLI):
- Create legal hold record: ./tools/legal-hold create --id INCIDENT-2027-001 --scope "logs, snapshots" --expires 2030-01-01

Log search example (SIEM):
- Query: index=auth_logs earliest=-30d | where actor="user:rajiv.kapoor@redwood.com" | stats count by action, outcome
